lesson.title: Arrive With Options
lesson.hook: Two connected choices. Watch what your first shot creates.
lesson.liveIntro: You spot the drop early. You arrive higher and more balanced, while they remain deep near the middle.

te1A.name: What does the passing shot offer now?
te1A.sit: They move forward and stretch across. Their pass comes higher through the middle.
te1A.q: What does the passing shot offer now?
opts: Keep a compact volley with controlled depth
Place a shorter volley into the open side

lines.A: A sound controlled volley. The higher ball also offered the shorter placement.
lines.B: You use the higher ball and open side. Keep covering until the point ends.

te1A.take: Earlier arrival creates options. Placement still depends on their position.
te1A.payoff: Earlier arrival creates options. Placement still depends on their position.
te1A.principle: Early arrival creates options. Place the ball, then stay ready.
te1A.why: Compared with the late pickup, earlier movement lets you contact the ball higher and closer to the net. With the opponent still deep, controlled shorter placement can make them move. It is not a winner by definition: organise for the pass they actually reach.

te1B.name: What does the passing shot offer now?
te1B.sit: Their comfortable contact sends the pass wider to your forehand. Adjust before volleying.
te1B.q: What does the passing shot offer now?
opts: Keep a compact volley with controlled depth
Place a shorter volley into the open side

lines.A: You adjust to the wider contact and keep a generous target.
lines.B: The placement lands here, but the wider contact makes it less forgiving.

te1B.payoff: Earlier arrival creates options. Placement still depends on their position.
te1B.principle: Early arrival creates options. Place the ball, then stay ready.
te1B.why: Compared with the late pickup, earlier movement lets you contact the ball higher and closer to the net. With the opponent still deep, controlled shorter placement can make them move. It is not a winner by definition: organise for the pass they actually reach.

te1.name: What has arriving early made available?
te1.sit: You spot the drop early. You arrive higher and more balanced, while they remain deep near the middle.
te1.q: What has arriving early made available?
opts: Place it shorter and away from their position
Send it deep back toward them

lines.A: Your placement brings them forward and across. Stay ready for their pass.
lines.B: They meet your deep pickup near their waiting position. Read the firmer pass.

summaries.10: The first choice fitted. The next ball needed a fresh decision.
summaries.11: Both choices fitted the contact and court you had. Keep reading as the point changes.
summaries.01: You adapted on the second ball. Compare what the first choice cost.
summaries.00: Compare the first choice, then read the next contact again. A landing alone does not prove a sound decision.

lesson.completionIntro: Your first choice changed the next ball. Read each contact afresh.
lesson.redoLabel: Try another route through this point

pro.label: Arrival · More control, more options
pro.moment: Tennis Australia’s tactical framework considers contact, balance and the opponent’s position together. Earlier arrival can change the available shot without deciding its target for you.
pro.read: Your next point: use the better arrival, then read their position. More time gives you a choice; it does not choose the shot.
pro.src: Tennis Australia · Technical and Tactical Fundamentals
pro.note: Coaching framework applied to this GameSharp point; no professional match is being recreated.

drill.name: Two-ball read
drill.how: Alternate a disguised drop with an obvious one. Let the receiver call “reach” or “options”, place the pickup, then play the real passing shot and next volley.
